name: Iter-RetGen - Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy (ITER-RETGEN)
venue: Findings of EMNLP 2023 (ACL Anthology 2023.findings-emnlp.620). Preprint arXiv:2305.15294 (cs.CL), v1 submitted 24 May 2023, v2 revised 23 Oct 2023.
authors_affiliation: Zhihong Shao (lead; The CoAI Group, DCST, Institute for Artificial Intelligence / State Key Lab of Intelligent Technology and Systems, Tsinghua University, Beijing), Minlie Huang (corresponding; Tsinghua University); Yeyun Gong, Nan Duan (Microsoft Research Asia); Yelong Shen, Weizhu Chen (Microsoft Azure AI). Primary affiliations: Tsinghua University and Microsoft.
code_url: N/A - no official first-party code release was found from the authors. Third-party reproductions exist (e.g., https://github.com/ictnlp/FlexRAG_Examples/tree/main/itrg). [uncertain]
task_domain: QA and knowledge-intensive reasoning - multi-hop open-domain question answering, fact verification, and commonsense reasoning (all cast as retrieval-augmented generation tasks).
problem_setting: Few-shot (3-shot in-context), single-agent, offline non-interactive inference with a fixed black-box LLM (text-davinci-003 / InstructGPT; also open-source Llama-2 in appendix). The setting is retrieve-and-read open-domain reasoning where retrievers struggle to capture relevance for queries with complex information needs (semantic gaps between the original question and its supporting knowledge). No LLM parameter updates; supervision is limited to 3 shared in-context demonstrations per dataset. An optional generation-augmented retrieval adaptation stage fine-tunes only the dense retriever's query encoder using ~9,000 train / 1,000 validation questions per dataset (HotPotQA, Feverous) and a re-ranker as teacher.
what_is_retrieved: Documents/paragraphs (Wikipedia passages) from an external knowledge corpus.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (per-dataset Wikipedia dumps indexed for dense retrieval). No agent-written growing/episodic memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k retrieval per query (top-5 paragraphs each iteration), but iteration is explicitly motivated by progressively accumulating a more comprehensive and relevant set of supporting knowledge across iterations (the authors note retrieval recall of gold paragraphs increases with iterations) - i.e., approximate completeness pursued via repeated fixed top-k retrieval rather than a single fixed ranking or a variable-size precision-driven recommendation.
retrieval_unit: document (Wikipedia paragraph/passage); top-5 paragraphs per retrieval call.
index_source: Static corpus constructed offline: per-dataset Wikipedia dumps (October 2017 dump for HotPotQA, December 2018 dump for 2WikiMultiHopQA, December 2021 dump for MuSiQue/Bamboogle/Feverous/StrategyQA), encoded for dense retrieval. Not test-time induced and does not grow online. (The retriever's query encoder can be optionally fine-tuned offline via generation-augmented adaptation, but the document store itself is static.)
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index (inner-product similarity over Contriever-MSMARCO embeddings); no graph or hierarchical structure.
retriever_type: Dense retriever (Contriever-MSMARCO, Izacard et al. 2022) - off-the-shelf bi-encoder; optionally adapted via distillation from a re-ranker (TART) in the generation-augmented retrieval-adaptation experiments.
retriever_learning_signal: Default: none (off-the-shelf Contriever-MSMARCO). Optional generation-augmented retrieval adaptation: the query encoder is trained by KL-divergence distillation from a re-ranker (TART) whose relevance scores are conditioned on the first-iteration LLM output y1 (i.e., LM-generation-conditioned re-ranker supervision distilled into the retriever). This is a distillation / LM-feedback signal, not contrastive similarity labels, RL, or human preference.
query_construction: First iteration: the raw question q is the query. Later iterations t>=2: the query is the concatenation of the previous-iteration LLM output y_{t-1} with the question q (y_{t-1} || q) - a full generation-augmented (generation-as-query) reformulation. The generated output is a Chain-of-Thought response that signals what knowledge is needed, used verbatim as retrieval context.
query_granularity: Iteration/trajectory-level (one query per iteration, formed from the whole previous generation plus the question), not per-CoT-step or per-token; one task-level query at t=1, then full-generation-conditioned queries at each subsequent iteration.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative on a fixed schedule: retrieval and a full generation alternate for a fixed number T of iterations (each iteration = retrieve-then-generate). No uncertainty trigger or learned router; T is a fixed hyperparameter (experiments report T=1..5, up to 7 iterations).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: exactly one retrieval at the start of each of the T iterations (retrieve top-5 using y_{t-1}||q, then generate a full output). No token-level confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, reflection tokens, or agent-initiated request; the number of iterations T is preset.
reranking: No reranking stage in the main inference loop (top-5 dense-retrieved paragraphs are used directly). A re-ranker (TART, Asai et al. 2022) is used only as a teacher during the optional offline generation-augmented retrieval-adaptation experiments (to distill into the retriever), not to rerank at inference.
retrieved_context_refinement: None at inference: all retrieved paragraphs are processed as a whole and prepended to the question; the paper explicitly contrasts this with DSP, deliberately NOT summarizing retrieved documents (to avoid summarization errors), and imposing no structural constraints / decomposition. No distractor filtering or compression.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the top-k retrieved paragraphs (D_{y_{t-1}||q}) are prepended to the question q in a Chain-of-Thought prompt, and the LLM generates a full reasoning+answer output y_t. All retrieved knowledge is processed as a whole within a single generation per iteration.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-generate per iteration in a fixed alternating loop (generation-augmented retrieval across iterations): each iteration produces a complete CoT output that is then reused as retrieval context for the next iteration. This is full-generation/whole-output interleaving, distinct from per-step (IRCoT), per-token (FLARE), or action-loop (ReAct) interleaving; no tree search, MCTS, or hierarchical subtask planning.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer / per-full-generation: retrieval is interleaved at the granularity of an entire model output (one complete CoT response per iteration), NOT per-CoT-step, per-sentence/token, or per-tool-call. This is the paper's defining distinction from token-level (FLARE) and CoT-step-level (IRCoT) interleaving.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved paragraphs (verbatim Wikipedia passage text with titles) injected into the prompt; not distilled, summarized, or converted to structured notes.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw document/paragraph (no abstraction or distillation of the retrieved unit).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Implicit/architectural rather than a dedicated module: processing all retrieved knowledge as a whole within a flexible CoT generation, and iterating, lets later iterations correct factual errors and override distractive paragraphs (case study shows distractor paragraphs in iteration 1 being corrected in iteration 2). The error analysis acknowledges that iteration-1 reasoning can be misled by noisy/distractive retrieved knowledge (65% of errors are retrieval-related). No retriever-aware SFT, explicit relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-aware training in the main method (the optional retrieval adaptation improves relevance but is not a noise-filtering module).
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory; only a per-question accumulation of retrieved paragraphs and the prior generation, which resets each question).
write_back: false - no new experiences/cases/skills are stored to a persistent memory across questions. (The optional retrieval-adaptation stage updates retriever parameters offline using generated outputs, but this is offline training, not online experience write-back.)
online_growth: false - the retrievable document store is fixed/frozen; it does not grow during deployment/test time.
write_back_trigger: never - no write-back to any persistent experience/case store occurs during inference. (Retriever adaptation is a separate, offline, one-time training procedure, not a per-deployment write trigger.)
failure_experience_usage: N/A - no failure or success experiences are stored or retrieved (no memory). Failures are only examined qualitatively in a manual error analysis (e.g., iteration-1 reasoning misleading retrieval), not fed back into any store.
memory_evolution_update: N/A - no stored experience entries to mutate (no memory). The only parameter update is the optional offline distillation of the retriever query encoder.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: false - retrieval is fixed dense top-5 (steered by the LLM's generated output as query). The optional generation-augmented adaptation trains the retriever's relevance/embedding (via KL distillation) but is not an RL/value-optimized retrieval-selection policy; selection remains similarity top-k.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A - single-model, single-agent; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.
benchmarks: HotPotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue (2-hop subset only), Bamboogle (multi-hop QA); Feverous (fact verification); StrategyQA (commonsense reasoning). Evaluated on 125 Bamboogle questions, first 500 StrategyQA train questions, and first 500 dev questions of the other datasets; 3-shot.
benchmark_family: QA / multi-hop (HotPotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle); fact verification (Feverous); commonsense reasoning (StrategyQA).
baselines: Without retrieval: Direct Prompting (Brown et al. 2020), CoT Prompting (Wei et al. 2022). With retrieval: Direct+retrieval, ReAct (Yao et al. 2022), Self-Ask (Press et al. 2022), and DSP (Khattab et al. 2022, on HotPotQA). Backend LLM: text-davinci-003 (InstructGPT); also Llama-2 in Appendix A. Retriever: Contriever-MSMARCO. Conceptually positioned against IRCoT (Trivedi et al. 2022) as another reasoning-retrieval synergy method.
key_metrics: Exact Match (EM) and F1 for multi-hop QA; Accuracy for fact verification (Feverous) and commonsense (StrategyQA); plus Acc-dagger, an LLM-judged (text-davinci-003) correctness metric that checks whether a prediction implies the gold answer (used because EM severely underestimates performance). Efficiency: average number of LLM API calls (#API) and number of retrieved paragraphs (#Doc). Retrieval recall of gold paragraphs is reported for the retrieval-recall analysis.
headline_result: ITER-RETGEN is superior to or competitive with state-of-the-art retrieval-augmented baselines (ReAct, Self-Ask, DSP) while incurring fewer retrieval and generation overheads. E.g., on HotPotQA ITER-RETGEN reaches EM 45.8 / F1 61.1 / Acc-dagger 73.4 (T=4) vs Self-Ask EM 36.8 / F1 55.2 / Acc-dagger 64.8; and ITER-RETGEN with only T=2 (2 API calls, 10 retrieved paragraphs total) is superior to or competitive with ReAct and Self-Ask (which use ~3 API calls and ~15 paragraphs). Generation-augmented retrieval adaptation further raises HotPotQA Acc-dagger to 75.7 at T=2 (vs 71.2 with the original retriever).
ablations: (1) Iteration count: increasing T from 1->5 (up to 7) generally improves all metrics, with the largest single boost at the second iteration; performance then plateaus (Table 2). (2) Generation-augmented retrieval adaptation (Table 4): distilling re-ranker (TART) knowledge into the dense query encoder using the first-iteration generation y1 improves Acc-dagger (HotPotQA T=2: 71.2 original -> 75.7 distilled w/ y1; Feverous T=1: 67.0 -> 70.7), and 'distilled w/ y1' beats 'distilled w/o y1', isolating the value of conditioning on the generation. (3) Parametric vs non-parametric knowledge breakdown (Table 5): on CoT-correct vs CoT-incorrect and answer-retrieved vs answer-not-retrieved subsets, ITER-RETGEN better preserves CoT-solvable cases and is consistently more accurate than Self-Ask whether or not retrieved knowledge mentions the answer - attributing Self-Ask's weakness to its structural (follow-up-question) constraints and inability to process all retrieved knowledge as a whole. (4) Efficiency comparison (Table 3): #API and #Doc vs ReAct/Self-Ask. (5) Metric analysis: manual check shows EM is 0 while Acc-dagger=1 for 98.75% of sampled cases, i.e., EM underestimates true correctness. (6) Error analysis: 65% of T=2 errors are retrieval-related (76.9% of those caused by wrong iteration-1 reasoning misleading retrieval), 10% correct-retrieval-but-wrong-reasoning, 25% false negatives. Appendix A reports Llama-2 results.
evaluation_decoupling: Partially: a separate retrieval-recall analysis reports that LLM generations help achieve significantly higher recall of gold supporting paragraphs (intrinsic retrieval metric), reported apart from end-to-end EM/F1/Acc-dagger task metrics; however the headline tables are end-to-end task metrics and no full Recall@k/nDCG table across all datasets is the primary report.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (EM/F1/Acc/Acc-dagger), but with process-oriented analyses: retrieval recall of gold paragraphs, a manual error analysis of where the retrieve-then-reason loop fails, and subset breakdowns by CoT-solvability and answer-retrieval - giving partial insight into intermediate retrieval/reasoning quality.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency is a central claim: ITER-RETGEN at T=2 uses exactly 2 LLM API calls and 10 retrieved paragraphs total (5 per iteration), versus ReAct (~2.1-3.0 API calls, ~10.6-15.0 docs) and Self-Ask (~2.3-3.2 API calls, ~11.3-16.0 docs) (Table 3), while achieving superior or competitive Acc-dagger - i.e., fewer retrieval and generation overheads for comparable/better accuracy. Each added iteration costs one more full LLM call plus one retrieval; gains plateau after a few iterations. [uncertain] exact dollar cost / wall-clock latency figures are not reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed top-k = 5 retrieved paragraphs per query/iteration (10 total at T=2, growing linearly with T as each iteration re-retrieves top-5 using the updated query). 3-shot demonstrations shared across methods. All retrieved paragraphs for the current iteration are prepended whole (no truncation/reranking budget). Backend models: text-davinci-003 and Llama-2.
builds_on: Chain-of-Thought prompting (Wei et al. 2022); few-shot in-context learning / GPT-3 / InstructGPT (Brown et al. 2020; Ouyang et al. 2022); retrieve-and-read open-domain QA; dense retrieval with Contriever-MSMARCO (Izacard et al. 2022); generation-augmented retrieval ideas - GAR (Mao et al. 2021), HyDE (Gao et al. 2022), and RepoCoder (Zhang et al. 2023, a 2-iteration retrieval-generation paradigm for code); re-ranking with TART (Asai et al. 2022) for the retrieval-adaptation distillation.
contrasts_with: Methods that interleave retrieval with generation WHILE producing a single output under structural constraints: Self-Ask (Press et al. 2022) and ReAct (Yao et al. 2022) (follow-up-question / action-observation decomposition), IRCoT (Trivedi et al. 2022, per-CoT-step retrieval), and FLARE-style token/sentence-level interleaving; and DSP (Khattab et al. 2022), which summarizes retrieved documents (risking summarization errors) - whereas ITER-RETGEN processes all retrieved knowledge as a whole, preserves generation flexibility without structural constraints, and uses the entire previous output as the next-iteration retrieval context.
lineage: Group B (retrieval-augmented task solving): an influential 2023 method establishing whole-generation-augmented iterative retrieval (generation-as-query at the full-output level) for knowledge-intensive multi-step reasoning, sitting alongside IRCoT (CoT-step interleaving) and FLARE (token-level active retrieval) and contrasting with action-loop ReAct/Self-Ask; a predecessor/comparison point for later iterative and adaptive RAG that condition retrieval on the model's own generations.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A - not a case-based reasoning method (no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle over solved problem-solution cases; it retrieves documents, not cases).
explicit_cbr_grounding: false - the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite CBR literature (Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner).
tool_document_engineering: N/A - no tools/skills are retrieved; only Wikipedia paragraphs are indexed (raw passage text encoded by a dense retriever).
index_content_separation: N/A - single flat dense paragraph index; no lightweight-index-then-content / progressive-disclosure separation.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A - no tool index or tool-integration protocol; static document corpus only.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A - no inter-tool dependency modeling (no tools).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A - not a CBR method; retrieved paragraphs are used verbatim as in-context evidence, not adapted as cases. (The closest 'adaptation' is the offline retriever query-encoder distillation, which adapts the retriever, not a retrieved case.)
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A - this is a method paper, not a survey/taxonomy.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A - this is a method paper, not a benchmark paper; it reuses existing datasets (HotPotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue 2-hop, Bamboogle, Feverous, StrategyQA), evaluating 125 Bamboogle questions, first 500 StrategyQA train questions, and first 500 dev questions of the other datasets under a shared 3-shot setting.
